reviews_highlighted.comment: I rarely leave negative reviews, but I feel compelled to share my experience, in hopes it helps others make an informed choice. During my root canal, the office used a mouthpiece that held my mouth open and constantly blew air while suctioning. I understand some offices use that technology, but for me it was extremely uncomfortable. It made my throat painfully dry, the noise was overwhelming, and after a while I started feeling panicked and claustrophobic. I’ve never experienced anything like that at another dental office. During the procedure, something appeared to go wrong. The dental assistant was still in training and seemed unsure, and the receptionist came into help. As a patient lying there, that did not inspire confidence. I was so uncomfortable, I decided not to return to that location and went to another office under the same company. Unfortunately, that experience also felt awkward and left me feeling like I’d made the wrong choice by returning. The one bright spot was Ann at the front desk. She was incredibly kind, patient, and helpful with my insurance questions. She even stepped in to help during my procedure when the assistant was still learning. Her professionalism, compassion, and customer service were outstanding, and she was truly a tremendous asset to the office. Unfortunately, my overall experience with the clinical care was so uncomfortable and disorganized that I won’t be returning. I hope the practice invests more in patient comfort, better communication, and making sure staff are fully trained and supported.

Please, please do not be misled by the high average reviews of this practice. 1 star feels…generous. I went here for a cleaning a month and a half ago and it was the worst dentist experience I’ve had. The dentist told me I had over 12 cavities before even examining me. My last x-rays were 9 months prior and I had no cavities. I don’t know if it’s because of the AI that they use or if they’re just trying to squeeze patients for money, but this was crazy to me. They told me they wanted me to come in four more times for four rounds of fillings, totaling over $1600 WITH insurance. The best part of this interaction? The dentist fully arguing with me, saying that I must never floss and have very poor dental hygiene. I don’t think I’ve gone a day without flossing & brushing in 15+ years, which I told him and he kept arguing that I definitely don’t floss. This was such a bizarre experience. I’ve never had a dentist accuse me of not flossing before, and I’ve NEVER had a practitioner argue with me like that. Just so bizarre😭

The cleaning I got was the worst I’ve ever had— it lasted ~5 minutes and left me with bruised gums and visible plaque still on my teeth. Maybe the dentist should’ve focused on cleaning my teeth instead of asking if I was interested in whitening treatments. So frustrating as my insurance covers two cleanings a year and this 100% was a waste of that coverage.

I told them very clearly I would be going elsewhere for future care because (1) their cost estimates are insane, (2) I truly cannot believe that I developed 12+ cavities in 9 months, and (3) the cleaning I received was shoddy at best.

I was going to let it go and not leave a harsh review, until I got a text recently. Over a month and a half after my visit, they contacted me saying that (without my consent) they contacted my insurance to ask for a pre authorization on the fillings that they previously suggested. I told them in no uncertain terms that I would not be coming back and I recall explicitly telling the receptionist to please make a copy of my x-rays to forward to my next dentist. I don’t know why they went behind my back to try to get me to return to their clinic— maybe they have a quota to fill. But I will definitely not be returning. Please avoid this place!! Trust the recent reviews and don’t believe the AI-generated responses she posts to each honest review!

The inconsistent information about my insurance wasted my time and made the entire experience frustrating. I expected transparency and accurate information before receiving care. I would recommend that anyone considering this office verify their insurance coverage independently and ask detailed questions about their treatment plan and scheduling before proceeding.

reviews_highlighted.comment: Dentist was very nice , kept me calm and very attentive. But the best part was the young lady Ms. Teerra Anderson ,she was very patient,polite and very informative!!! After my visit I had more question and she explained EVERYTHING from the payment to the treatment!!  She was quite knowledgeable about my treatment I didn’t have to speak with my dentist!!!! It’s very rare that you’ll find someone in her profession who is sincerely nice and cares!! Thanks again.

I have been a patient at Downtown Dental (Loop) for 15+ years and up until now, my experiences with them have always been positive.  Over the past year and a half, I have been living in Delaware but since I was back in Chicago in December I decided to schedule an appointment for a routine cleaning.  When I arrived at my appointment I was not experiencing any issues, so I was quite surprised when Dr. Abou-Hanna informed me that in addition to the three "spots" they had been keeping an eye on, there were three new ones.  And I was told that they now needed to be filled.  Considering I am in my late 40s, have only had one cavity up until this point, and pay extra for fluoride treatments at every cleaning, you could say I was a bit shocked.  In hindsight, I wish I had told her that I wanted to get a second opinion before proceeding with fillings since there was no mention of any cavity concerns at a dental appointment in DE just 8 months prior.  But hindsight is 20/20, and when Dr. Abou-Hanna said that it would be better to take care of them now than to deal with root canals later, I panicked and agreed to get the four on my left side taken care of that day.  What a mistake that was.

For the next six weeks I had a great deal of sensitivity in the area where the fillings were done by Dr. Abou-Hanna, so I made an appointment with my dentist in DE.  At that appointment, I was told that one of the teeth marked in Downtown Dental's ledger as having been filled was completely bare.  There was nothing there, which was likely the source of my sensitivity.  I was also told that there are no signs of cavities on my right side - not even any spots to watch.  Hmmm - that's interesting.  What happened to the two noted by Dr. Abou-Hanna in my Dec visit?  Leads me to wonder how necessary the ones I had done on my left side really were.

The DE Dentist was willing to fill the tooth for me but since I get back to Chicago periodically she suggested I might want to first follow-up with Downtown Dental since I had already paid for that filling.  So I sent an email to Downtown Dental that afternoon requesting that Dr. Abou-Hanna follow-up with me once she had a chance to take a look a photo of the tooth (taken by DE dentist).  A staff member responded to my email and said that she would forward the image to Dr. Abou-Hanna for review. I thanked her and said I was looking forward to hearing back. When I hadn't heard back three days later, I reached out again.  Three days later, still no response.  I understand things can get busy but when a patient is experiencing pain as a result of work performed in your office, SOMEONE should follow-up.

It seems like there has been a change in ownership or something because like I said before, my experiences with Downtown Dental up until this point were always positive.  Can't say that now.
Downtown dental has some of the best hygienist and dentists I’ve experienced. Dr. Ken and Dr. Noor were fantastic, thorough and extremely knowledgeable. Thank you!

Dr Amy Koblinska has been my dentist since I moved to Chicago. She’s the absolute best and I wouldn’t rather have another dentist. Professional and down to Earth. She’s been handling my Invisalign like a pro! She’s the heart of Downtown Dental!

Went in for the $79 comprehensive exam promotion. Determined that I had stage 1 periodontitis. They quoted >$2000 for deep cleaning + laser therapy. Can't afford that so I had to find another dentist. However, as far as service goes, this place is nice. When I asked to get the medical records, they also delivered everything in email the same day with no fuss.

Don't beg for an appointment; you are an important client, and they work—and put food on their tables—thanks to you.

I called them more than 15 times—with the insurance agent waiting on the other end of the line each time—and they kept putting me on hold. I was never able to schedule an appointment because they were unable to validate my insurance. They offer no solutions; if this is how things start out, I dread to imagine what the actual service must be like.

The most humiliating experience. Just bring the cash if you want them to work.

Booked a “complimentary” orthodontist appointment. (I was there before with an emergency visit, and even had to buy a discount plan for $99). On the website there’s no information about the consultation requirements + I texted them and talked on the phone about it. Here’s the date and time, no fee. Okay…

And today at the appointment time after 10 minutes waiting for the doctor, they told me: we can’t do a consultation without a full exam, and brought me a bill to pay. The reason is “to make sure you have no cavities”. What if I do? No consultation available?

I just wanted to talk to a doctor and to learn more about Invisalign. And yes, it makes sense to check the X-rays – I have the most recent ones and never been asked for them.

I am upset how rude they refused to give me the consultation, waisting my time and not saying anything in advance.

After 20 years as a patient, twice a year, I’m done. They scheduled me for a cleaning without a hygienist on staff, wasted an hour of my time, and treated me poorly throughout the visit with no cleaning done . I won’t be returning.
